speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having a chronic wound on your right lower leg; can you tell me how long it has been present and what you believe might have caused it?

speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history of chronic swelling and a prior DVT is very suggestive of venous insufficiency. Have you noticed any varicose veins, skin discoloration (staining) around the ankle, or ulcers on your feet?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Large wound on the right lower leg. I also have Chronic leg swelling, Family history of similar leg problems. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Venous Insufficiency (likely with venous stasis ulceration), supported by history of DVT, chronic bilateral leg swelling, and family history of similar pathology.
